sessions.answer_excerpt: A Rust trait object is a dynamically-typed reference (like `&dyn Trait` or `Box<dyn Trait>`) that allows you to work with different types that implement the same trait through a single pointer, enabling runtime polymorphism.

A Rust trait object is a dynamically dispatched pointer (like `&dyn Trait` or `Box<dyn Trait>`) that lets you work with any type implementing a trait without knowing the concrete type at compile time.

A trait object is a dynamically-dispatched reference to any type implementing a trait, allowing you to store and call trait methods on different types at runtime through a single pointer (e.g., `&dyn Trait` or `Box<dyn Trait>`).
A Rust trait object is a dynamically-dispatched reference (like `dyn Trait`) that can point to any concrete type implementing that trait, enabling polymorphism at runtime.

A Rust trait object is a dynamically-dispatched reference (like `&dyn Trait` or `Box<dyn Trait>`) that lets you store or pass different concrete types as long as they all implement the same trait, with method calls resolved at runtime rather than compile time.
